fields.label: Rate limits
fields.description: Two fixed-window counters guard this server. One is per person, so a runaway agent cannot starve anyone else. One is shared by everyone, so the site itself cannot be hammered. A refusal is answered with a Retry-After and costs nothing further. Every read this server makes goes to the read replica, so a burst never touches the database the CRM writes to.

fields.label: Window (seconds)
fields.description: The period both counts are expressed over. A count resets when the window rolls over.

fields.label: Per-person calls per window
fields.description: How many calls one person's assistant may make in a window. An agent answering one question typically makes three or four. 0 removes this limit.

fields.label: Total calls per window
fields.description: How many calls everyone together may make in a window — the ceiling that protects the site. 0 removes this limit, which is not recommended on a live site.

fields.label: Answer size
fields.description: How much one answer may carry. These bound what a single call can cost to build and to read: an assistant asks again for the next page rather than being handed everything at once.

fields.label: Handbook results per search
fields.description: How many pages a handbook search returns. Each carries a title, a route and a short snippet.

fields.label: Schema results per search
fields.description: How many doctypes, and how many fields, a schema search returns.

fields.label: Characters per page of a document
fields.description: How much of a long handbook page comes back at once. The answer says how many pages there are, and the assistant asks for the next one by number.
